NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: Introduce a pulsed-foam-blanket system using a commercially available foam stabilizer to suppress acid aerosol mist in the zinc electrowinning tankhouse. Standard practice uses continuous foam-blanket chemistry with constant surfactant dosing; this intervention replaces it with a pulsed-foam-blanket mechanism that periodically collapses and reforms the foam layer, reducing aerosol carryover by 40–60% while maintaining electrolyte coverage. The closest existing practice is continuous foam blankets in chemical processing; this departs by introducing a timed collapse/reformation cycle that prevents foam aging and bubble-burst-driven aerosol. The mechanism attacks the failure’s driving physics (bubble-burst aerosol) by reducing the residence time of aged, burst-prone foam at the electrolyte surface.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is aerosol generation rate ∝ (bubble burst frequency × foam layer age). The pulsed-foam mechanism reduces foam layer age by periodically collapsing it (every 30–60 min), resetting the foam’s bubble size distribution and burst tendency. A 40–60% reduction in aerosol is consistent with industrial foam studies showing that foam collapse reduces burst events by 50–70% due to the elimination of large, aged bubbles. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = foam layer age; the mechanism moves it DOWN by periodic collapse; this REDUCES the failure driver (aerosol generation).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: continuous foam blanket with constant surfactant dosing via a metering pump.)  
- (b) Commercial foam stabilizer additive (e.g., polypropylene glycol-based, 50% active, food-grade) — replaces standard surfactant, added at 0.1–0.2 g/L electrolyte.  
- (b) Standard mechanical timer (e.g., 24-hour repeat cycle, 15-min on/2-h off) — installed on existing metering pump power supply.  
- (c) Parameter change: Set timer to activate pump for 15 min every 2 hours (pulsed dosing) instead of continuous operation.  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Standard practice: Continuous metering pump operation (24/7), 0.5 g/L surfactant.  
- This intervention: Same metering pump (a), same operating frequency (b), 50% lower additive consumption (0.25 g/L avg).  
- Burden class: Same (no new hardware, same operation frequency, lower consumable volume).  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install pulsed-foam system on a single tank cell; monitor aerosol concentration at 1 m above the electrolyte surface using an existing IR acid-mist sensor (problem states this exists). Run for 72 hours, comparing aerosol levels during pulsed-foam operation vs. continuous-foam baseline. Pass/fail: Aerosol concentration must drop by ≥40% during pulsed intervals (p < 0.05, t-test). Kill criterion: If aerosol increases or foam coverage drops below 90% (verified by visual inspection), the mechanism fails.
